ud8.6:0.2: The Discourse about the Pāṭali Villagers
ud8.6:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was walking on walking tour amongst the Magadhans with a great Community of monks, and arrived at Pāṭaligāma.
ud8.6:1.3: The lay followers of Pāṭaligāma heard:
ud8.6:1.4: “The Fortunate One, it seems, is walking on walking tour amongst the Magadhans with a great Community of monks, and has arrived at Pāṭaligāma.”
ud8.6:1.5: Then the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma went to the Fortunate One, and after going and worshipping the Fortunate One, they sat down on one side.
ud8.6:1.6: While sat on one side the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma said this to the Fortunate One:
ud8.6:1.7: “May the Fortunate One consent, reverend Sir, to (stay in) our rest house.”
ud8.6:1.8: The Fortunate One consented by maintaining silence.
ud8.6:2.1: Then the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma, having understood the Fortunate One’s consent, after rising from their seats, worshipping and circumambulating the Fortunate One, went to their rest house, and after going, and spreading (the mats) so that the rest house was spread all over, and preparing the seats, setting up the water-pot, and lighting the oil-lamp, they went to the Fortunate One, and after going and worshipping the Fortunate One, they stood on one side. While stood on one side the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma said this to the Fortunate One:
ud8.6:2.2: “The rest house is spread with mats all over, reverend Sir, the seats are prepared, the water-pot is set up, and the oil-lamp is lit,
ud8.6:2.3: now is the time for whatever the Fortunate One is thinking, reverend Sir.”
ud8.6:3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having dressed, after picking up his bowl and robe, together with the Community of monks, went to the rest house, and after going, washing his feet, and entering the rest house, he sat down near to the middle pillar, facing the East,
ud8.6:3.2: and the Community of monks, having washed their feet, and entering the rest house, sat down near the West wall, facing the East, having the Fortunate One at the front.
ud8.6:3.3: Also the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma, having washed their feet, entered the rest house, sat down near the East wall, facing the West, having the Fortunate One at the front.
ud8.6:3.4: Then the Fortunate One addressed the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma, (saying):
ud8.6:4.1: “There are these five dangers, householders, for one lacking in virtue, for one who has lost his virtue.
ud8.6:4.3: Here, householders, one lacking in virtue, one who has lost his virtue, because of being heedless undergoes a great loss of riches.
ud8.6:4.4: This is the first danger for one lacking in virtue, for one who has lost his virtue.
ud8.6:5.1: Furthermore, householders, for one lacking in virtue, for one who has lost his virtue, a bad report goes round.
ud8.6:5.2: This is the second danger for one lacking in virtue, for one who has lost his virtue.
ud8.6:6.1: Furthermore, householders, one lacking in virtue, one who has lost his virtue, whatever assembly he goes to, whether an assembly of nobles, or an assembly of brāhmaṇas, or an assembly of householders, or an assembly of ascetics, he goes without confidence, with confusion.
ud8.6:6.2: This is the third danger for one lacking in virtue, for one who has lost his virtue.
ud8.6:7.1: Furthermore, householders, one lacking in virtue, one who has lost his virtue, dies bewildered.
ud8.6:7.2: This is the fourth danger for one lacking in virtue, for one who has lost his virtue.
ud8.6:8.1: Furthermore, householders, one lacking in virtue, one who has lost his virtue, at the break up of the body, after death, arises in the lower world, in an unhappy destiny, in the fall, in the nether regions.
ud8.6:8.2: This is the fifth danger for one lacking in virtue, for one who has lost his virtue.
ud8.6:8.3: These are the five dangers, householders, for one lacking in virtue, for one who has lost his virtue.
ud8.6:9.1: There are these five advantages, householders, for one who is virtuous, for one accomplished in virtue.
ud8.6:9.3: Here, householders, one who is virtuous, one accomplished in virtue, because of being heedful obtains a great mass of riches.
ud8.6:9.4: This is the first advantage for one who is virtuous, for one accomplished in virtue.
ud8.6:10.1: Furthermore, householders, of one who is virtuous, of one accomplished in virtue, a good report goes round.
ud8.6:10.2: This is the second advantage for one who is virtuous, for one accomplished in virtue.
ud8.6:11.1: Furthermore, householders, one who is virtuous, one accomplished in virtue, whatever assembly he goes to, whether an assembly of nobles, or an assembly of brāhmaṇas, or an assembly of householders, or an assembly of ascetics, goes with confidence, without confusion.
ud8.6:11.2: This is the third advantage for one who is virtuous, for one accomplished in virtue.
ud8.6:12.1: Furthermore, householders, one who is virtuous, one accomplished in virtue, dies without being bewildered.
ud8.6:12.2: This is the fourth advantage for one who is virtuous, for one accomplished in virtue.
ud8.6:13.1: Furthermore, householders, one who is virtuous, one accomplished in virtue, at the break up of the body, after death, arises in a happy destiny, in a heavenly world.
ud8.6:13.2: This is the fifth advantage for one who is virtuous, for one accomplished in virtue.
ud8.6:13.3: These are the five advantages, householders, for one who is virtuous, for one accomplished in virtue.”
ud8.6:14.1: Then the Fortunate One, after instructing, rousing, enthusing, and cheering the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma for most of the night with a Dhamma talk, dismissed them, (saying):
ud8.6:14.2: “The night has passed, householders, now is the time for whatever you are thinking.”
ud8.6:14.3: Then the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma, after greatly rejoicing and gladly receiving this word of the Fortunate One, rising from their seats, worshipping and circumambulating the Fortunate One, went away.
ud8.6:14.4: Then the Fortunate One, not long after the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma had gone, entered an empty place.
ud8.6:15.1: Then at that time the Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra were building up a city at Pāṭaligāma to ward off the Vajjians.
ud8.6:15.2: Then at that time a great many devatās, thousands upon thousands, were taking possession of grounds at Pāṭaligāma.
ud8.6:15.3: In that place where the great devatās took possession of grounds, there the powerful rulers’ and great royal ministers' minds inclined to building up residences.
ud8.6:15.4: In that place where the middling devatās took possession of grounds, there the middling rulers’ and middling royal ministers' minds inclined to building up residences.
ud8.6:15.5: In that place where the lower devatās took possession of grounds, there the lower rulers’ and lower royal ministers' minds inclined to building up residences.
ud8.6:16.1: The Fortunate One saw with his divine-eye, which is purified, and surpasses that of (normal) men, that those devatās, thousands upon thousands, were taking possession of grounds at Pāṭaligāma.
ud8.6:16.2: In that place where the great devatās took possession of grounds, there the powerful rulers’ and great royal ministers' minds inclined to building up residences.
ud8.6:16.3: In that place where the middling devatās took possession of grounds, there the middling rulers’ and middling royal ministers' minds inclined to building up residences.
ud8.6:16.4: In that place where the lower devatās took possession of grounds, there the lower rulers’ and lower royal ministers' minds inclined to building up residences.
ud8.6:16.5: Then towards the time of dawn, having risen from his seat, the Fortunate One addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
ud8.6:17.1: “Now who, Ānanda, is building a city at Pāṭaligāma?”
ud8.6:17.2: “The Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra, reverend Sir, are building up a city at Pāṭaligāma to ward off the Vajjians.”
ud8.6:17.3: “It is just as though, Ānanda, after consulting with the Tāvatiṁsa devas,
ud8.6:17.4: in the same way, Ānanda, the Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra, are building up a city at Pāṭaligāma to ward off the Vajjians.
ud8.6:17.5: Here, Ānanda, I saw with my divine-eye, which is purified, and surpasses that of (normal) men, that a great many devatās, thousands upon thousands, were taking possession of grounds at Pāṭaligāma.
ud8.6:17.6: In that place where the great devatās took possession of grounds, there the powerful rulers’ and great royal ministers' minds inclined to building up residences.
ud8.6:17.7: In that place where the middling devatās took possession of grounds, there the middling rulers’ and middling royal ministers' minds inclined to building up residences.
ud8.6:17.8: In that place where the lower devatās took possession of grounds, there the lower rulers’ and lower royal ministers' minds inclined to building up residences.
ud8.6:17.9: For as long, Ānanda, as there is an Ariyan sphere (of influence), for as long as there is trade, this basket-opening Pāṭaliputta will be the chief city.
ud8.6:17.10: For Pāṭaliputta, Ānanda, there will be three dangers:
ud8.6:17.11: from fire and from water and from the breaking of an alliance.”
ud8.6:18.1: Then the Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra went to the Fortunate One, and after going, they exchanged greetings with the Fortunate One
ud8.6:18.2: and after exchanging courteous talk and greetings, they stood on one side.
ud8.6:18.3: While stood on one side the Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra said this to the Fortunate One:
ud8.6:18.4: “May Gotama consent, dear Sir, to us (offering him) a meal today, together with the Community of monks.”
ud8.6:18.5: The Fortunate One consented by maintaining silence.
ud8.6:19.1: Then the Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra having understood the Fortunate One’s consent, went to their own dwelling, and after going, in their own dwellings having had excellent comestibles and edibles made ready, announced the time to the Fortunate One,
ud8.6:19.2: (saying): “It is time, dear Gotama, the meal is ready.”
ud8.6:20.1: Then the Fortunate One, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up his bowl and robe, together with the Community of monks, went to the dwelling of the Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra, and after going, he sat down on the prepared seat.
ud8.6:20.2: Then the Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra with their own hands served and satisfied the Community of monks with the Buddha at its head with excellent comestibles and edibles.
ud8.6:21.1: Then the Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra, when the Fortunate One had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, having taken a low seat, sat down on one side.
ud8.6:21.2: While sat on one side the Fortunate One rejoiced the Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra with these verses:
ud8.6:22.1: “In that place where he makes his dwelling,
ud8.6:22.3: The wise and virtuous here, ~ the restrained,
ud8.6:23.1: He should dedicate a gift to the devatās who are in that place.
ud8.6:23.3: Honoured, they pay honour, ~ revered, they revere him.
ud8.6:24.1: Thereafter they have compassion on him,
ud8.6:24.2: ~ as a mother on her own son,
ud8.6:24.3: A man whom the devatās have compassion on ~ always sees what is auspicious.”
ud8.6:25.1: Then the Fortunate One after rejoicing the Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra with these verses, and rising from his seat, went away.
ud8.6:26.1: Then at that time the Magadhan chief ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra were following close behind the Fortunate One, (thinking):
ud8.6:26.2: “That gate by which the ascetic Gotama leaves will get the name the Gotama Gate,
ud8.6:26.3: and that ford by which he crosses the river Gaṅgā will get the name the Gotama Ford.”
ud8.6:27.1: Then that gate by which the Fortunate One left got the name the Gotama Gate,
ud8.6:27.2: then the Fortunate One went to the river Gaṅgā.
ud8.6:27.3: Then at that time the river Gaṅgā was full to the brim, and could be drunk from by crows (perched on the bank).
ud8.6:27.4: Some of the people were seeking boats, some were seeking floats, and some were binding rafts, desiring to go from this shore to the shore beyond.
ud8.6:27.5: Then the Fortunate One, just as a strong man might stretch out a bent arm, or bend in an outstretched arm, so did he vanish from the near bank of the river Gaṅgā, and reappeared on the far bank, together with the Community of monks.
ud8.6:28.1: The Fortunate One saw those people, some seeking boats, some seeking floats, and some binding rafts, desiring to go from this shore to the shore beyond.
ud8.6:29.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud8.6:30.1: “Those who cross over a sea or a lake,
ud8.6:30.2: (Do so) after making a bridge, and leaving the pond behind.
ud8.6:30.3: (While) people are still binding together a raft,
